topic: smart-home anomaly detection; encrypted-traffic inference; cross-app privacy chains
status: bounded comparison of three heterogeneous full-text sources (2020, 2022, 2025); two-study follow-up audit is partial; shared benchmark and external validation absent
claim: IoTGaze, HomeGuardian, and PrivacyGuard address related smart-home risks but measure different tasks: encrypted ZigBee metadata to event/anomaly inference, Home Assistant logs plus temporal/environment context to classify forged events, and modeled trigger-condition-action chains to estimate privacy leakage. Their accuracy/F1/chain percentages cannot be ranked or pooled. HomeGuardian's prose headline says F1 exceeds .90 for every device, but its extracted table reports temporal-context-only F1 from .33 to .91 across device rows and has malformed column headers; that discrepancy requires checking the publisher PDF before using a single cross-device headline. PrivacyGuard extends cross-app privacy-chain analysis over larger rule/app datasets and has an official artifact-reproduced badge, but does not validate IoTGaze's specific candidate physical-channel chains. The shared gap is independently adjudicated transfer/false-alarm performance under held-out homes, devices, protocol loss, and real attack scenarios.

sources.title: IoTGaze: IoT Security Enforcement via Wireless Context Analysis
locators: five device types, 19 event types, injected anomaly metrics

official artifact status: Available, Functional, Reproduced

interpretation: The papers motivate a shared multi-site evaluation protocol but are not direct replications: they use different sensor modalities, threat models, labels, and outputs. The HomeGuardian table observation is provisional pending PDF column-layout verification; PrivacyGuard's artifact badge should not be overstated as independent replication.
falsifiable_question: On a shared, independently annotated multi-home scenario suite, how do wireless-metadata event inference, log/context anomaly detection, and app-chain privacy analysis transfer across held-out sites/devices and realistic packet loss/outages, and what are their respective false-alarm, missed-attack, and expert-confirmed chain rates?
primary_outcome: Per-site/vendor/protocol precision and recall; false alarms per home-day; missed naturally occurring and seeded events; detection latency; expert-confirmed/rejected/untestable chain rate; robustness to packet loss and service downtime; compute and setup cost.
counterevidence_and_caveats: IoTGaze and HomeGuardian report strong outcomes under their own declared setups; this synthesis does not show either system fails there.
HomeGuardian's extracted HTML table has malformed headers; verify publisher PDF before asserting which classifier column yields each per-device F1.
PrivacyGuard's artifact status records artifact evaluation and does not independently reproduce the scientific result.
PrivacyGuard's two-app privacy-leak percentage is not comparable to IoTGaze's candidate physical-interaction chains.
None is a direct replication of the other, and the proposed shared benchmark has not been run.
Global novelty and real-world prevalence are unresolved.

confidence.privacyguard_reported_scope_and_artifact: high as stated by official proceedings

suggested_design: Create a consented multi-site smart-home testbed with held-out homes/vendors/protocols; retain raw encrypted packet traces and platform logs; predeclare benign, malfunction, injected, and naturally observed threat labels. Evaluate each system only on compatible inputs, but share event ground truth. Blind independent security assessors to the method output when judging exploitability of app chains. Freeze thresholds on validation homes, report full confusion matrices and subgroup rates, and independently inspect official paper tables/artifacts before adopting aggregate claims.
